content:
The image shows two banana fruits on a white background. Key visual features:

- **Affected part**: Banana fruits (fingers)
- **Lower banana**: Shows large, black, sunken lesions covering much of the fruit surface — dark brown to black discoloration with sunken areas
- **Upper banana**: Shows some yellowing/greening with scattered small dark spots developing
- **Lesion characteristics**: The black areas appear sunken and irregular, consistent with post-harvest rot/decay on the fruit skin
- **No powdery grey coating** (ruling out Cigar End Rot, which would show ash-like conidia at the tip)
- **No tip-focused blackening** (ruling out Cigar End Rot)
- The lesions are distributed across the fruit body, black and sunken — matching Anthracnose description

Comparing to classes:
- **Anthracnose**: "Black and sunken lesions on banana fruits, with spore masses or acervuli visible in the lesions" — this matches perfectly. The dark, sunken, spreading lesions on the fruit skin are characteristic of Anthracnose.
- **Cigar End Rot**: Would show blackening specifically at the tip/perianth end with powdery grey ash-like appearance — not what is seen here.
- All other classes (Sigatoka, Panama Disease, Bunchy Top, Cordana Leaf Spot) affect leaves or the whole plant, not fruit surfaces in this pattern.
